name: Spit
description: Spit (or 'Slam') is a fast-paced two-player shedding card game related to Speed. Unlike Speed, each player maintains five small 'stock piles' in front of them (similar to Solitaire layout) and races to empty these piles onto two central discard stacks. Play is simultaneous and chaotic. The winner of a round gets to choose the smaller pile for the next round, aiming to start with fewer cards.

content.text: Spit (or 'Slam') is a fast-paced two-player shedding card game related to Speed. Unlike Speed, each player maintains five small 'stock piles' in front of them (similar to Solitaire layout) and races to empty these piles onto two central discard stacks. Play is simultaneous and chaotic. The winner of a round gets to choose the smaller pile for the next round, aiming to start with fewer cards.
Likely developed alongside Speed in the mid-20th century. The name 'Spit' refers to the action of flipping the top card onto the active pile.
Two players only. Play is simultaneous with no turns; physical speed and alertness are required to play faster than the opponent.
Standard 52-card deck. Shuffle well and divide the pack equally so each player receives 26 cards; no jokers.

Shuffle and divide the deck equally (26 cards each). Each player deals five stock piles in a row: first pile 1 card, second 2, third 3, fourth 4, fifth 5. Deal face down then turn the top card of each pile face up. The remaining 11 cards per player stay face down as the spit cards.

items.text: Four stock piles: Some play with only four stock piles containing one, two, three and four cards each.
Alternate colour on spit piles: Some play that cards on the spit piles must alternate in colour (e.g. on a black 5 only a red 6 or red 4 may be played).
